findings.title: Posting a year-end adjustment is impossible in production — the endpoint writes columns that do not exist and omits two NOT NULL ones, and it bypasses the posting kernel
findings.evidence: apps/api/routers/year_end_adjustments.py:504-532 builds `journal_entry = {id, firm_id, entry_date, reference_no, narration, "source": "YEAR_END_ADJUSTMENT", "source_ref_id": adjustment_id, is_posted, created_at}` and then does `db.table("journal_entries").insert(journal_entry)` followed by a separate `db.table("journal_lines").insert(journal_lines)`. journal_entries has no `source` and no `source_ref_id` column — apps/api/tests/fixtures/production_schema_2026-09-03.json lists exactly ['attachments','client_id','created_at','created_by','deleted_at','entry_date','entry_type','firm_id','id','is_posted','is_reversed','narration','posted_at','posted_by','rate_*','reference_no','reversal_of','source_id','source_type','status','updated_at'] — so PostgREST rejects the statement at parse time. Even with those removed, `client_id` and `entry_type` are NOT NULL (apps/api/migrations/003_phase3a_foundation.sql:122 and :126) and neither is supplied. The two inserts are also not atomic and do not go through phase2_journal_service._create_journal, contradicting docs/architecture/01-accounting-engine.md's "There are no alternative posting paths". The frontend button is live: apps/web/app/clients/[id]/year-end/[engagementId]/adjustments/_page.tsx:109 calls yearEndApi.adjustments.post, wired at apps/web/lib/api/yearEnd.ts:310. Tests are green because they run against an in-memory FakeDB that accepts any column: apps/api/tests/test_r240_year_end_critical_gaps.py:324-341 asserts `len(db.rows("journal_entries")) == 1`, and apps/api/tests/_backend_query_parser.py:230 only inspects inline `ast.Dict` payloads, so `.insert(journal_entry)` (a variable) is invisible to tests/test_backend_columns_exist_pg.py.
findings.ca_experience: The CA does the whole year-end: creates the closing adjustments (provisions, prepaid, depreciation top-up, accrued interest), routes them through draft → submitted → approved, clicks Post, and gets a 500 with no useful message. The adjustment stays 'approved' forever and NONE of it reaches the ledger, so the signed Balance Sheet and P&L are the unadjusted trial balance. Nothing on screen says the ledger was not touched.
findings.market_standard: In TallyPrime year-end adjusting entries are ordinary journal vouchers and post like any other. Zoho Books posts manual journals with the same engine as invoices. Winman/CompuTax take the finalised trial balance and expect the adjustments to already be in the books.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the direct inserts and call phase2_journal_service._create_journal(db, firm_id, existing['client_id'], existing['adjustment_date'], f'YEA-{adjustment_id[:8].upper()}', existing['description'], 'Journal', lines, is_posted=True, source_type='year_end_adjustment', source_id=adjustment_id, created_by=current_user['id']). Then add a real-Postgres test that posts an adjustment against the migration-built schema, because the FakeDB test cannot catch this class.

findings.title: Cash receipts and cash vendor payments are posted to the Bank ledger — Cash in Hand never moves
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/phase2_journal_service.py:210 `bank_id = self._find_account(db, firm_id, client_id, "%Bank%", system_key="bank")` in receipt_journal_lines, and :766-769 the same in journal_for_purchase_payment (`Cr Bank Account = amount_paise`). apps/api/services/receipt_service.py:178 does the same on the atomic settlement path. `payment_mode` IS captured and stored (production schema receipts.payment_mode; apps/api/services/purchase_payment_service.py:180 `"payment_mode": data.get("payment_mode", "bank")`) but grep shows it is never consulted when choosing a GL account. The UI offers cash explicitly: apps/web/app/clients/[id]/purchases/page.tsx:2219 `{["bank","cash","cheque","upi","neft","rtgs"].map(...)}`. 'Cash in Hand' (1001) and 'Petty Cash' (1002) are seeded at apps/api/services/coa_seed_service.py:56-57 and no automatic flow ever posts to them.
findings.ca_experience: An SME client pays a vendor ₹40,000 in cash. The CA selects mode 'cash'; the journal credits Bank Account. The bank ledger is now ₹40,000 short of the passbook and will never reconcile, while Cash in Hand shows nil despite a real cash box. On the Balance Sheet, Cash & Cash Equivalents is right in total but wrong in composition, and the cash-flow statement's operating cash is derived from the same wrong ledger.
findings.market_standard: Tally's Payment/Receipt voucher makes you pick the exact cash or bank ledger — it is the credit leg of the voucher, not a metadata field. Zoho Books, Busy and Marg all require you to name the deposit-to / paid-through account and refuse to save without it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `payment_account_id` (FK to chart_of_accounts, or bank_accounts.coa_account_id) to receipts and purchase_payments, default it from payment_mode ('cash'/'petty cash' → system_account_key 'cash'), and make the journal use it. Backfill is not needed for correctness of new entries; existing rows keep the generic bank leg and should be listed for the CA rather than silently re-pointed.

findings.title: Every receipt and vendor payment posts to one generic "Bank Account" ledger, while bank-statement entries post to the correct per-bank ledger
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/bank_posting_service.py:87-91 resolves the real ledger — `db.table("bank_accounts").select("coa_account_id")` and returns `ba["coa_account_id"]` — falling back to the generic `%Bank%` only at :104. But apps/api/services/phase2_journal_service.py:210 and :766-769 (receipts and vendor payments) go straight to `_find_account(..., "%Bank%", system_key="bank")`, which is one firm-wide account. The `receipts` table has no bank_account_id at all (apps/api/tests/fixtures/production_schema_2026-09-03.json: receipts columns are allocated_paise, amount_paise, client_id, customer_id, …, payment_mode, …, no bank reference), while bank_accounts DOES carry coa_account_id, and apps/api/services/opening_balance_service.py:250-256 posts each bank's opening balance into its own coa_account_id.
findings.ca_experience: A client with HDFC and ICICI accounts: the ICICI opening balance and every ICICI statement line land in the ICICI GL ledger, but every receipt and vendor payment recorded from the invoice screens lands in a third, generic 'Bank Account' ledger. No individual bank ledger agrees with its passbook, the Balance Sheet shows three bank lines where the client has two banks, and per-account bank reconciliation cannot be tied to the GL.
findings.market_standard: Tally, Zoho Books and Busy all make the bank ledger the actual credit/debit leg of the voucher, so the ledger balance IS the bank balance and BRS runs per account.
findings.suggested_fix: Same fix as ACC-02 — one `payment_account_id` on receipts/purchase_payments resolved from the chosen bank account's coa_account_id. Then make bank_posting_service and the receipt/payment paths share one resolver so they cannot diverge again.

findings.title: An auto-posted journal (sales invoice, purchase bill, payroll, depreciation) can be edited through the manual-journal edit endpoint, decoupling the GL from its source document
findings.evidence: apps/api/routers/accounting.py:452-490 `PATCH /api/accounting/journal/{entry_id}` calls manual_journal_service.update for ANY entry the caller can reach; apps/api/services/manual_journal_service.py:185-297 checks is_reversed and the period lock but never source_type; the SQL it delegates to, `edit_posted_journal` (apps/api/migrations/266_editable_journals_until_locked_or_filed.sql, the `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.edit_posted_journal` body), checks firm, client, deleted_at, is_reversed, both dates against the period lock and Dr=Cr — and does not look at source_type either. The DELETE path deliberately does: apps/api/migrations/275_discard_manual_journal_until_locked.sql:82 `IF COALESCE(v_entry.source_type, '') <> 'manual' THEN` … 'an auto-posted journal is corrected by correcting its document, or the document is left pointing at nothing'. No test asserts the auto-posted case is allowed — apps/api/tests/test_r266_journal_edit_until_locked_pg.py:107 and tests/test_journal_edit_until_locked.py:130 seed only `source_type='manual'`.
findings.ca_experience: An executive opens the journal behind a sales invoice by URL, changes the revenue account or the amount, and saves. The GL now says one thing and client_sales_invoices says another. GSTR-1 is built from the invoice rows and the books from the GL, so the return and the trial balance stop agreeing with nothing recording why — and the AR sub-ledger (paid_paise/status) no longer ties to the Trade Receivables control account.
findings.market_standard: Tally will not let you alter the accounting entry of a voucher independently of the voucher — you alter the voucher and the entry follows. Zoho Books makes system-generated journals read-only entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same `source_type = 'manual'` guard to edit_posted_journal that discard_posted_journal already has (and mirror it in manual_journal_service.update so the CA gets the sentence rather than a SQLSTATE). Reuse migration 275's wording verbatim.

findings.title: A client's financial year, once locked by finalising the year-end engagement, can never be reopened — there is no unlock path anywhere
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/phase2_journal_service.py:1566-1579 refuses every posting into a locked client year with the message 'Reopen the year before posting to it.' The lock is written by apps/api/services/year_end_workflow_service.py:61-66 → year_lock_service.set_client_lock(..., lock=True). year_lock_service.set_client_lock supports lock=False (apps/api/services/year_lock_service.py:141-147) but grep across apps/api shows the only caller is year_end_workflow_service with lock=True, and grep across apps/web finds no reference to client_year_locks at all. The engagement itself is terminal: apps/api/routers/year_end.py:91-96 `_STATUS_TRANSITIONS` maps `"locked": []`. The FIRM-level lock, by contrast, has a working unlock (routers/accounting.py:614 `POST /year-lock` with lock=false, screen at apps/web/app/accounting/lock-year/page.tsx).
findings.ca_experience: The Partner finalises FY 2025-26 for a client on 20 September. On 5 October the bank sends a revised interest certificate, or a §143(1) intimation forces a correction. Every posting to that client for that year is refused, the engagement cannot leave 'locked', and there is no screen or API to reopen it. The only remedies are a direct SQL DELETE on client_year_locks or posting the correction into the wrong year.
findings.market_standard: Tally's period lock is set and cleared by an authorised user at will. Zoho Books lets an admin unlock a closed period with a reason. Every Indian practice reopens a closed year at least once a season — revised returns, audit adjustments, ITR filing findings.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Partner-gated, audited `DELETE /api/year-end/{engagement_id}/lock` (or a `locked → approved` transition) that calls set_client_lock(lock=False) with a mandatory reason, and surface it on the year-end dashboard. The audit row already exists in set_client_lock; only the entry point is missing.

findings.title: Recurring journals, budgets and retainers are stored in browser localStorage — not in the database, not shared, not automatic
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/accounting/recurring/page.tsx:40-53 `const LS_KEY = "practicesync_recurring_templates"` with loadTemplates/saveTemplates reading and writing localStorage; the only posting is a manual 'Post Now' button (:250-270) that stamps `entry_date: today` rather than the template's due date, and deleteTemplate (:242-247) just filters the local array. apps/web/app/accounting/budget/page.tsx:35-51 keeps every budget figure under a per-FY localStorage key. apps/web/app/accounting/retainer/page.tsx:80-115 keeps retainers, work log and generated invoices in three localStorage keys. All three are advertised as firm registers on the Accounting hub: apps/web/app/accounting/page.tsx:19-22 ('Recurring Transactions — Automate monthly, quarterly & yearly entries', 'Budget vs Actuals', 'Retainer Tracker').
findings.ca_experience: A Manager sets up twelve recurring journals (rent, depreciation, director's remuneration, interest accrual) on the office desktop. The Partner opens the same screen at home and sees nothing. Clearing site data, switching browsers or re-imaging the machine loses them all with no export. Nothing posts on schedule — the word 'Automate' on the hub card is not true. Budget-vs-actual variance is meaningless because the budget half lives on one person's laptop.
findings.market_standard: Tally has memorandum and recurring vouchers in the company data file. Zoho Books has recurring journals with a real schedule and auto-post. Busy and Marg both store recurring entries server-side. Budgets in Tally are per-company data, visible to every user.
findings.suggested_fix: Give recurring templates, budgets and retainers real firm-scoped tables with RLS, move the CRUD behind API endpoints with rbac(), and post due templates from jobs/scheduler.py as DRAFTS (the scheduler already refuses to auto-post — apps/api/jobs/scheduler.py:228 — so drafts into the approval queue is the shape that fits). Until then the hub cards should say 'this device only'.

findings.title: The Audit Log screen shows only the 200 most recent firm-wide rows and cannot show one entry's edit history — the Rule 3(1) edit log is written but not usable
findings.evidence: apps/api/routers/audit.py:18 `limit: int = Query(50, le=200)` caps the endpoint at 200; apps/web/app/settings/audit-log/page.tsx:205 `const FETCH_LIMIT = 200` and :225 `api.audit.list({ limit: FETCH_LIMIT })` — every date, action, entity and user filter at :251-260 is applied client-side over those 200 rows, and there is no pagination or cursor. The endpoint accepts `entity_id` (routers/audit.py:17) but the page never passes it, and neither the journal list nor the journal editor (apps/web/components/journal/JournalEditor.tsx) links to it. Volume makes this acute: apps/api/migrations/266_…sql attaches `trg_audit_capture_line` AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE on journal_lines, so every posting writes one audit row per line, and apps/api/services/audit_service.py's header records 46,311 audit_log rows already measured in production.
findings.ca_experience: During an audit the CA is asked 'who changed this entry, and from what to what?' The Audit Log page shows the last 200 events — typically a few hours of one active client — with no way to search back, no date-range server filter, and no way to pull the history of one journal entry. The bulk-delete confirmation even tells them deleted entries 'stay in Settings → Audit Log with their lines', which is true in the table and false on the screen.
findings.market_standard: TallyPrime's Edit Log is per-voucher: open a voucher and see every version with the before/after of each field, plus a whole-company Edit Log report filterable by date, user and voucher type. That is the control the Companies (Accounts) Rules proviso is written for, and it is the parity target.
findings.suggested_fix: Add server-side date/entity/actor filtering and keyset pagination to GET /api/audit, then add a 'History' tab on the journal entry page that calls it with entity_type=journal_entry&entity_id={id} and renders the journal_line create/update/delete rows as a before/after diff. The data is already there; only the query and the screen are missing.

findings.title: The Trial Balance is always inception-to-date — choosing a financial year only moves the as-at date, so revenue and expense rows accumulate across every prior year
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/reporting/service.py:218-233 `def trial_balance(self, firm_id, client_id, as_of_date, basis)` takes no start date and calls `self.source.snapshot(firm_id, client_id, None, as_of)` / `_passbook_accrual_lines(firm_id, client_id, None, as_of)`. apps/api/routers/accounting.py:895-911 exposes only `as_of_date`. The screen renders an FY period picker but discards the start: apps/web/app/clients/[id]/accounting/page.tsx:1151-1157 computes `period` then :1158 `const asOf = period.end;` and :1176 calls `api.accounting.trialBalance({ basis, as_of_date: asOf, client_id })`. There are no year-end closing entries in the product either — the Balance Sheet synthesises retained earnings instead (apps/api/domain/reporting/builders.py:506-517 `net_profit = income_net - expense_net` over all balances, labelled 'Retained Earnings / Net Profit') — so nothing ever zeroes the P&L accounts.
findings.ca_experience: In year two, a CA picks 'FY 2026-27' on the Trial Balance and gets Sales of ₹1.9 crore when the year's sales were ₹80 lakh, because FY 2025-26's ₹1.1 crore is still in the row. Grand debit still equals grand credit, so it looks correct; the CA who reconciles the TB to the P&L finds a difference they cannot explain. Every Schedule III and tax working built off that TB is wrong.
findings.market_standard: Tally's Trial Balance is period-scoped (F2 sets the period; balance-sheet accounts carry opening + period movement, P&L accounts show only the period). Zoho Books' Trial Balance takes a date range. Winman and CompuTax expect a year's trial balance as input.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `start_date` to ReportingService.trial_balance and the endpoint, pass `period.start` from the screen, and present balance-sheet accounts as opening + movement + closing while P&L accounts show the period's movement only. The passbook (account_period_balances) is already monthly, so the fast path needs no new data.

findings.title: The chart of accounts is flat, and there is no screen anywhere to create or edit a single ledger
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/coa_seed_service.py:52-113 seeds 53 accounts with no parent_id and no group column values. `parent_group`/`sub_group` were added by apps/api/migrations/057_coa_architecture_correction.sql:5-6 and grep shows NO backend code writes them; the only writer is the CSV importer, apps/web/app/accounting/coa-import/page.tsx:171. The Account Groups screen groups by exactly those columns — apps/web/app/accounting/account-groups/page.tsx:66-74 `const pg = acc.parent_group ?? "Ungrouped"; const sg = acc.sub_group ?? "General"` — so for a normally-seeded firm it renders one 'Ungrouped → General' block. `parent_id` is accepted by POST /accounts (apps/api/routers/accounting.py:125) but nothing reads it (grep for parent_id across apps/api returns only the select list at routers/accounting.py:83 and an unrelated banking probe). And no screen calls the create endpoint: `createAccount` is defined at apps/web/lib/api/index.ts:728 and referenced nowhere else in apps/web; `updateAccount` at :729 likewise. The only way to add an account is to import a whole CSV chart.
findings.ca_experience: A CA needs one new ledger — 'Director's Remuneration' — mid-year. There is no 'New Account' button on any screen. They must build a CSV with the right headers and run the CoA import. And because the chart has no group hierarchy, the Balance Sheet cannot be drilled by group and the Account Groups screen shows everything as 'Ungrouped'.
findings.market_standard: Tally's whole model is 28 primary groups with user sub-groups, and Alt+C creates a ledger inline from any voucher field without leaving the entry. Zoho Books, Busy and Marg all have a Chart of Accounts screen with New/Edit and a parent-account picker.
findings.suggested_fix: Two separate pieces of work: (a) a Chart of Accounts screen with create/edit wired to the existing POST/PATCH /api/accounting/accounts (and an inline 'create account' in AccountLookup, which is where a CA actually needs it); (b) decide whether groups are `parent_id` (self-referencing, Tally-shaped) or `parent_group`/`sub_group` (text, import-shaped) and make ONE of them authoritative — today both exist and neither is used.

findings.title: The Schedule III Mapping screen changes nothing — the statements bucket by account_subtype substring and year-end uses a third, different table
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/accounting/schedule-iii-mapping/page.tsx reads and displays `chart_of_accounts.schedule_iii_mapping` (:47) and tells the CA to 'Set schedule_iii_mapping during import (Import COA) to assign a mapping' (:93). Grep across apps/api shows NO Python reads schedule_iii_mapping. The statutory statements bucket by free-text substring on account_subtype instead: apps/api/domain/reporting/schedule_iii.py:26-80 `bs_bucket` does `sub = (account_subtype or "").lower()` and matches 'payable', 'inventor', 'term loan', 'receivable' etc. The year-end statements use yet a third mechanism, the `account_group_mappings` table (apps/api/services/year_end_financial_service.py:392, :502-505; apps/api/routers/year_end_statements.py:365). apps/api/services/coa_seed_service.py:38-47 itself flags the fragility: 'A subtype that doesn't contain the keyword its account's own Schedule III line needs silently falls into a generic "Other …" bucket … there is no shared/enforced vocabulary between the two.'
findings.ca_experience: The CA spends an afternoon on the Schedule III Mapping screen and the Balance Sheet does not change by a rupee. Worse, the screen shows a green count ('37 of 53 active accounts mapped') that implies the mapping is doing something. Meanwhile an account whose subtype happens not to contain the magic substring lands in 'Other Current Assets' with no warning.
findings.market_standard: Tally maps to Schedule III through the group hierarchy, which is one structure the user actually controls. Winman and CompuTax import a trial balance and ask the CA to map each ledger to a Schedule III line once, and that mapping is what drives the statements.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one classification source. The most defensible is chart_of_accounts.schedule_iii_mapping (an explicit CA decision) with account_subtype as the fallback: make bs_bucket/pl_bucket read the mapping first, make the mapping screen writable, and reconcile account_group_mappings into it so the year-end statements and the live Balance Sheet cannot disagree.

findings.title: POST /api/accounting/accounts cannot set account_subtype, so every account a CA creates lands in a generic "Other …" Schedule III caption
findings.evidence: apps/api/models/accounting.py:19-25 `class AccountIn` has name, code, account_type, parent_id, description, is_active — no account_subtype. apps/api/routers/accounting.py:117-127 writes firm_id, client_id, account_code, account_name, account_type, parent_id, is_active and nothing else. apps/api/models/accounting.py:35-39 `AccountUpdateIn` allows only name, code, description, is_active — and routers/accounting.py:184-196 rejects anything else, so subtype, type and parent cannot be changed after creation either. Schedule III presentation then falls through to the catch-alls at apps/api/domain/reporting/schedule_iii.py:57 ('Other Current Liabilities'), :79 ('Other Current Assets').
findings.ca_experience: A CA creates 'Security Deposits (Asset)' through the API. On the Balance Sheet it appears under Other Current Assets instead of Long-term Loans & Advances, and there is no way to correct it — the PATCH endpoint answers 'Only name, code and is_active can be changed on an account.' The only route to a correct subtype is to delete nothing (you cannot) and re-import the chart.
findings.market_standard: Tally makes you choose the group at creation and lets you regroup later. Zoho Books asks for the account type and sub-type at creation and both are editable.
findings.suggested_fix: Add account_subtype (and parent_id) to AccountIn/AccountUpdateIn and to the router's write payloads, validated against the vocabulary bs_bucket/pl_bucket actually recognises. That vocabulary should become a shared constant so the two cannot drift.

findings.title: A filed return locks EDITING a period but not POSTING into it — the two halves of the same rule are enforced on different paths
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/period_lock_service.assert_open (the filed-return gate, backed by public.period_lock_reason from apps/api/migrations/267_period_lock_reason_for_every_document.sql) is called from exactly two files: routers/sales_invoices.py:825, :1252-1254 and routers/purchase_bills.py:1345-1347. Creating a NEW manual journal checks only the firm FY lock — apps/api/services/manual_journal_service.py:92 `period_validation_service.validate_posting_date(firm_id, entry_date)`. The kernel checks only the CLIENT year lock (apps/api/services/phase2_journal_service.py:1566-1579). So posting a draft (journal_posting_service.py:104), reversing (routers/accounting.py:786), bank entries, payroll, fixed-asset depreciation, credit/debit notes, receipts, payments, opening balances and trial-balance import all reach a period whose GSTR-3B is filed. Separately, only GST returns ever write the `filings` table that the lock reads — apps/api/services/gst_filing_record_service.py:134-149 is the sole writer (grep), so a filed ITR or TDS return locks nothing even though migration 266's own comment names 'GSTR-1/3B, ITR, TDS'.
findings.ca_experience: GSTR-3B for June is filed on 20 July. On 25 July the CA tries to fix a June journal and is refused with a clear sentence. On the same day they post a NEW June journal and it goes through silently. The books behind a filed return move without anything recording it, and the asymmetry reads as a bug in whichever direction the CA hits first.
findings.market_standard: Tally's period lock blocks both new vouchers and alterations in the locked range. Zoho Books' closing date blocks all transactions dated on or before it.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the filed-return check into phase2_journal_service._create_journal beside the client year-lock check, so one gate covers every posting path exactly as the year-lock comment argues. Make it a warning-with-override for postings (a CA legitimately posts a July correction into June before amending) but keep it a hard refusal for edits. Separately, record ITR and TDS filings in `filings` so the lock covers what its message claims.

findings.title: No day book, no cost centres, no bill-wise references, no party ledgers in the GL
findings.evidence: grep -rni 'day.?book|cost cent|cost_cent|bill.?wise|bill_wise' across apps/api and apps/web returns one unrelated comment (apps/api/domain/banking/splits.py:7). The Journal tab shows manual entries only — apps/web/app/clients/[id]/accounting/page.tsx:647-650 `const visibleEntries = useMemo(() => entries.filter((e) => e.source_type === "manual"), [entries])` — so there is no chronological view of every voucher. Parties are not ledgers: customers and vendors are separate master tables and every sale posts to one 'Trade Receivables' control account (apps/api/services/phase2_journal_service.py:78-80, coa_seed_service.py:58), so the GL cannot show a party-wise ledger; the party view exists only as customer_statement_service.
findings.ca_experience: A CA who has used Tally for fifteen years opens the product and cannot find the Day Book — the screen they live in. They cannot ask 'what did we post on 14 August', cannot allocate an expense to a branch or partner (no cost centres), and cannot answer 'which of this vendor's five bills does this ₹2 lakh payment settle' from the ledger (bill-wise references) — only from the allocation tables behind the payment screen.
findings.market_standard: Day Book (D in Tally's Display menu) is Tally's most-used report. Cost centres and cost categories are core Tally and present in Busy and Marg. Bill-wise details (New Ref / Agst Ref / Advance / On Account) is how every Indian practice ages a party balance and is the reason CAs trust Tally's outstandings.
findings.suggested_fix: Day book is cheap and high-value: one screen over journal_entries with no source_type filter, grouped by date, with entry_type as the voucher-type column — the data and the paging helper already exist. Cost centres and bill-wise references are structural (a dimension column on journal_lines; a reference table keyed to documents) and belong in a planned phase, not a side effect of another task.

findings.title: Opening balances cover only aggregate AR, aggregate AP and bank — every other account, and every party- or bill-level opening, needs the CSV trial-balance import
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/opening_balance_service.py:219-244 `_plan_opening` computes exactly three targets: `ar_total = _sum_opening(customers)` posted to one `%Trade Receivable%` account, `ap_total = _sum_opening(vendors)` posted to one `%Trade Payable%`, and per-bank amounts to each bank's coa_account_id, contra'd to Opening Balance Equity. Legs are `AR, AP, BANK = "ar", "ap", "bank"` (:155). Nothing brings forward fixed assets, accumulated depreciation, inventory, loans, capital, reserves, statutory dues or prepaid balances — those come only from apps/api/services/trial_balance_import_service.py, which posts a separate journal family (`TB_SOURCE = "TrialBalance"`, :70) and creates accounts from CSV names.
findings.ca_experience: Migrating a live client from Tally, the CA enters party and bank opening balances on the masters and gets a Trade Receivables total but no per-party opening ageing, and a Balance Sheet missing fixed assets, loans and capital until they separately build and import a trial balance CSV. The two mechanisms are not reconciled against each other, so it is easy to double-count a bank balance that appears in both the master and the imported TB.
findings.market_standard: Tally takes opening balances per ledger and, for parties, bill-by-bill with dates — which is what makes day-one ageing correct. Zoho Books' migration wizard takes opening balances for every account plus open invoices and bills individually.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the trial-balance import the single opening-balance path (it already handles any account), and have the master opening_balance_paise fields feed party-level opening DOCUMENTS (open invoices/bills with dates) rather than a control-account total — that is what gives day-one ageing. Add a reconciliation screen that shows the TB import and the master totals side by side before either posts.

findings.title: A discarded draft journal can be resurrected and posted, because post_draft never selects deleted_at
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/journal_posting_service.py:31-33 `_SELECT = ("id, entry_date, reference_no, narration, entry_type, is_posted, status, source_type, source_id, created_by, created_at, posted_at, posted_by, journal_lines(...)")` — no `deleted_at` and no `client_id`. The guard at :89 `if je.get("deleted_at"): raise HTTPException(409, ...)` is therefore always false, and :116 `timeline_service.log(je.get("client_id"), ...)` always passes None. Discarding a draft only sets deleted_at (apps/api/routers/accounting.py:583-585). The resulting entry is is_posted=true with deleted_at set, so apps/api/migrations/228_account_period_balances_triggers.sql `apb_on_entry_post` skips it (`AND NEW.deleted_at IS NULL`) and apps/api/domain/reporting/sources.py:382 excludes it — a posted entry that is in no report.
findings.ca_experience: A CA deletes a draft journal, then approves the same id from a stale approval-queue tab (or a retried request). The API reports success, the entry flips to Posted, and it appears in no report and no balance — a row whose state contradicts itself. The timeline event for every draft approval is also written with a null client and never surfaces on the client's timeline.
findings.market_standard: Any workflow tool refuses to approve a deleted item. Tally has no draft/approve split, but Zoho Books will not publish a deleted draft journal.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `deleted_at, client_id` to _SELECT (one-line change) — the guard and the timeline call then work as written. A regression test that discards a draft and then calls post_draft would have caught it.

findings.title: Journal lines have no ordering column, so a voucher's Dr/Cr lines display in arbitrary order and an edit reshuffles them
findings.evidence: journal_lines carries no sequence column — apps/api/tests/fixtures/production_schema_2026-09-03.json lists account_id, base_currency, created_at, credit_paise, debit_paise, exchange_rate, id, journal_entry_id, narration, rate_date, rate_source, rate_type, txn_credit, txn_currency, txn_debit, and `id` defaults to a random uuid (migrations/003_phase3a_foundation.sql:140). apps/api/services/manual_journal_service.py:145-149 selects `lines:journal_lines(id, account_id, debit_paise, credit_paise, narration)` with no .order(). apps/api/migrations/266_…sql's edit_posted_journal does `DELETE FROM public.journal_lines WHERE journal_entry_id = p_entry_id` then re-inserts, so every correction can re-order the lines.
findings.ca_experience: A CA opens a five-line journal and the debits and credits appear interleaved in a different order each time, and in a different order from the one they typed. On a compound entry (salary accrual: gross Dr, PF/ESI/TDS/net Cr) that makes the voucher hard to read and hard to check against the working paper.
findings.market_standard: Tally preserves voucher line order exactly as entered, and prints it that way. Zoho Books keeps journal line order.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `line_no INT NOT NULL` to journal_lines, populate it in post_journal_atomic and edit_posted_journal from the array index, backfill existing rows by created_at then id, and order every read by it.

findings.title: Reporting endpoints aggregate across the WHOLE firm when client_id is omitted, for a caller who is only assigned some clients
findings.evidence: apps/api/routers/accounting.py:869-881 records it in the code itself: 'client_id is checked when named; when omitted, every reporting endpoint below aggregates across the WHOLE FIRM rather than narrowing to the caller's own assigned clients — "accounting" read is _AT_LEAST_EXECUTIVE, not Partner-only, so this is a live gap for a non-firm-wide caller who simply omits client_id. Recorded, not fixed.' It applies to /ledger, /trial-balance, /profit-loss, /balance-sheet, /schedule-iii and /cash-flow (:895, :937, :957, :975, :1197). By contrast /journals (:640-645) and /ledger-span (:923-929) DO narrow via effective_client_ids, so the inconsistency is inside one router.
findings.ca_experience: An Executive assigned to three clients calls GET /api/accounting/trial-balance with no client_id and receives the consolidated trial balance of every client in the practice — turnover, salaries, loans, bank balances. Nothing in the UI does this, so it needs a deliberate request; but the endpoint is reachable with an ordinary staff token.
findings.market_standard: Any multi-client practice tool scopes reports to the user's assigned client list. Zoho Practice and Jamku both enforce per-client staff assignment on every report.
findings.suggested_fix: Thread effective_client_ids through ReportingService (ledger/trial_balance/profit_loss/balance_sheet/schedule_iii/cash_flow) and both its Supabase and mock sources — the router comment already scopes the work. As an interim, refuse an omitted client_id for non-firm-wide roles, which is a guard rather than a rewrite.

findings.title: The Lock Financial Year screen offers a hardcoded list of years ending at 2025-26 — the current year cannot be locked
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/accounting/lock-year/page.tsx:39-44 `const FY_LIST = [{label:"2025-26"...},{"2024-25"},{"2023-24"},{"2022-23"}]` and :249 `{FY_LIST.map((fy) => {` is the only source of the rows. The backend has no such limit — apps/api/routers/accounting.py:610-627 accepts any FYLabel and apps/api/services/year_lock_service.py:47-95 stores an arbitrary array. The current Indian FY on today's date (2026-09-07) is 2026-27, which is absent, as is 2025-26's successor for every future year.
findings.ca_experience: A Partner wanting to lock FY 2026-27 after finalising it cannot: the year is not in the list. The same screen also cannot UNLOCK a year that was locked by a client-level workflow, and it silently rots one more year every 1 April.
findings.market_standard: Tally's period lock takes any date. Zoho Books' closing date is a date picker.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the list from the current FY (core/ist_clock.ist_fy_label's frontend twin already exists in lib/workspace/ClientNavContext.getCurrentFinancialYear) — the current year plus the previous six — or read the client's ledger span from GET /api/accounting/ledger-span, which exists for exactly this problem.

findings.title: Multi-currency is fully built across five phases but cannot be switched on for any firm or client from the product
findings.evidence: apps/api/domain/currency/policy.py:47-56 requires three gates: `l1 = multi_currency_platform_enabled()` (apps/api/core/feature_flags.py:15-21, 'OFF (the default)'), `l2 = firm.multi_currency_entitled`, `l3 = client.multi_currency_enabled`. Grep across apps/web finds NO reference to multi_currency_enabled, multi_currency_entitled or functional_currency; grep across apps/api/routers finds only SELECTs (routers/currencies.py:63,69; routers/banking.py:171-173; routers/sales_invoices.py:699-700; routers/purchase_bills.py:687-688; routers/purchase_payments.py:583-584) — no endpoint writes either flag. Behind the gate sit ~770 lines of domain/currency plus fx_revaluation_service, five FX report views (routers/fx_reports.py) and a gated UI tab (apps/web/app/clients/[id]/accounting/page.tsx:242-253).
findings.ca_experience: A CA with an export client asks for foreign-currency invoicing. The FX Reports tab is invisible, every posting is refused as INR-only by the kernel gate (apps/api/services/phase2_journal_service.py:1597-1602), and there is no setting anywhere to enable it — the only route is direct SQL against firms and clients.
findings.market_standard: Zoho Books enables multi-currency from Settings with one toggle. Tally's 'Enable multi-currency' is an F11 feature. Both are self-service.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Partner-gated PATCH to set firms.multi_currency_entitled and clients.multi_currency_enabled, surfaced in firm settings and the client profile, and document that MULTI_CURRENCY_ENABLED must also be true in the environment. Nothing in the accounting logic needs to change.

findings.title: A legacy PATCH /api/accounting/journal/{id}/post is still mounted, Partner-callable, and backed by the in-memory demo engine
findings.evidence: apps/api/routers/accounting.py:735-763 `post_journal_entry` calls `accounting_service.post_journal_entry(entry_id)` — the module-level in-memory store at apps/api/domain/accounting_service.py (its MOCK_ACCOUNTS list at :31 is the same store routers/accounting.py:53-77 documents as 'THIS USED TO SERVE DEMO DATA TO EVERY FIRM AND CLIENT'). It is reached regardless of SUPABASE_URL. The frontend already knows: apps/web/app/clients/[id]/accounting/journal/[entryId]/edit/_page.tsx:158-160 'the legacy PATCH /journal/{id}/post is backed by the in-memory engine and would not touch this client's ledger at all.'
findings.ca_experience: Nobody in the UI hits it, but it is a Partner-permissioned endpoint that reports success against a shared in-process store — so an integration or a retried request can be told a journal was posted when nothing reached the ledger, and it writes a real audit_log 'approve' row and a real timeline event for a posting that did not happen.
findings.market_standard: Not applicable — this is dead code, and the standard is that it should not be reachable.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the route and its `_assert_journal_scope` helper. POST /api/accounting/journals/{id}/post (:718-733) is the real path and is what the frontend calls.

findings.title: post_journal_atomic validates the entry's firm and client but never checks that the LINE accounts belong to that firm
findings.evidence: apps/api/migrations/271_post_journal_atomic_security_definer.sql:103-123 checks `(p_entry->>'firm_id')::uuid IS DISTINCT FROM v_my_firm`, `public.can_access_client(p_entry->>'client_id')` and the internal-client Partner rule — all on the ENTRY. The line insert at :166-186 takes `(l->>'account_id')::uuid` with no validation at all, and journal_lines' only constraint is a global FK to chart_of_accounts(id) (apps/api/migrations/003_phase3a_foundation.sql:142). manual_journal_service.create (apps/api/services/manual_journal_service.py:96-101) passes account_ids straight through. The one account-level guard that does exist is trg_archived_account_check (referenced in apps/api/migrations/266_…sql's header), which blocks inactive accounts, not foreign-firm ones.
findings.ca_experience: Not something a CA reaches through the UI (AccountLookup is firm-scoped), but a crafted API call with another firm's account uuid posts a line against it. The consequence is a corrupt ledger for the caller's own client — the account resolves to nothing in their chart, so apps/api/domain/reporting/builders.py:19 `_acc` falls back to showing the raw uuid as the account name, and an account_period_balances bucket is created against a chart row the firm does not own.
findings.market_standard: Every ledger engine validates that a voucher's ledgers belong to the company being posted to; it is a foreign-key within the tenant, not across tenants.
findings.suggested_fix: In post_journal_atomic and edit_posted_journal, assert every account_id exists in chart_of_accounts with firm_id = the entry's firm and (client_id = the entry's client OR client_id IS NULL). One EXISTS check per statement; it also closes the case of posting to a different client's account within the same firm.

findings.title: No drill-through from a ledger line to the voucher behind it
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/clients/[id]/accounting/page.tsx:1071 `getRowId={(l) => l.entry_id}` — the journal entry id is present on every ledger row and used only as a React key. The ledger columns defined at :994-1013 (Date, Particulars, Ref, Debit, Credit, Balance) carry no link, and the journal entry route (/clients/{id}/accounting/journal/{entryId}/edit) exists and takes exactly that id. The API already returns it: apps/api/domain/reporting/builders.py:57 `"entry_id": e.id`.
findings.ca_experience: Reviewing Trade Receivables, the CA sees a ₹4.2 lakh debit with a reference they do not recognise and has no way to open it. They copy the reference, switch to the Journal tab (which shows manual entries only), fail to find it, and give up or go to the Sales tab and search by hand.
findings.market_standard: Tally: Enter on a ledger-vouchers line opens the voucher; Enter again drills to the entry. QuickBooks and Zoho Books both make every report amount a link to its source transaction.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the ledger row clickable, routing to the journal entry page for a manual entry and to the source document (source_type/source_id are already stamped on the entry) for an auto-posted one.

findings.title: No year-end closing process: the P&L is never transferred to reserves and the FY 'close' only sets a lock
findings.evidence: apps/api/services/year_end_workflow_service.py:24-66 `lock_year_if_completing` is the whole of what closing a year does — `set_client_lock(..., lock=True)`. No closing journal is posted anywhere (grep for 'Retained Earnings' across apps/api returns only the seed at coa_seed_service.py:81 and the SYNTHETIC balance-sheet line at domain/reporting/builders.py:512). The Balance Sheet computes retained earnings on the fly: builders.py:506-517 `income_net = sum(-net for ...is_income); expense_net = sum(net for ...is_expense); net_profit = income_net - expense_net` labelled 'Retained Earnings / Net Profit' with a synthetic account_id '__retained__'.
findings.ca_experience: The Balance Sheet is arithmetically right, but the Retained Earnings figure is a computed line with no ledger behind it, so it cannot be drilled into, cannot be split between reserves and current-year profit as Schedule III requires, and cannot receive appropriations (proposed dividend, transfer to general reserve, partners' profit-sharing). For a partnership or LLP there is no way to allocate the year's profit to partners' capital accounts at all.
findings.market_standard: Tally computes the P&L account balance the same way (no closing entry) but exposes it as a real ledger you can drill and appropriate against. Zoho Books posts a closing entry to Retained Earnings at year end. Every Indian firm expects to allocate profit to partners' capital.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an optional year-end closing/appropriation step to the year-end engagement that posts a real balanced journal (Dr revenue, Cr expenses, Cr/Dr Retained Earnings, then appropriations to capital or reserves) through the kernel, dated the FY end, and make the Balance Sheet stop synthesising the line once a closing entry exists for the year — otherwise it would double count.

findings.title: The Account Groups screen renders nothing useful for a normally-onboarded firm
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/accounting/account-groups/page.tsx:66-74 groups by `acc.parent_group ?? "Ungrouped"` then `acc.sub_group ?? "General"`. Those two columns exist (apps/api/migrations/057_coa_architecture_correction.sql:5-6) but the firm seed never sets them — apps/api/services/coa_seed_service.py:117-140 `seed_firm_coa` writes only firm_id, client_id, account_code, account_name, account_type, account_subtype, is_active. Grep confirms the only writer of parent_group/sub_group in the whole repo is apps/web/app/accounting/coa-import/page.tsx:169-170.
findings.ca_experience: A CA opens Account Groups expecting a Tally-style tree and sees one block, 'Ungrouped → General', containing all 53 accounts. The header even reports '1 parent groups · 53 active accounts'. It reads as a broken screen rather than an unused feature.
findings.market_standard: Tally's group tree IS the chart of accounts. Busy and Marg both present a group hierarchy as the primary CoA view.
findings.suggested_fix: Either populate parent_group/sub_group in coa_seed_service.STANDARD_COA (a fourth tuple element, cheap and immediately useful), or fold this screen into the Chart of Accounts screen ACC-09 asks for. Do not leave both.

findings.title: The journal editor never sends attachments, though the kernel, the model and the database all support them
findings.evidence: apps/api/models/accounting.py:102 `attachments: list[dict] = []  # supporting documents: [{"name","url"}, ...]`; apps/api/services/manual_journal_service.py:115 passes `attachments=data.get("attachments") or []` to the kernel; apps/api/services/phase2_journal_service.py:1661-1662 writes them onto the entry; journal_entries.attachments is a NOT NULL jsonb defaulting to '[]' in the production schema fixture. apps/web/components/journal/JournalEditor.tsx:139-165 `buildPayload()` returns only entry_date, entry_type, reference_no, narration and lines, and the editor has no upload control.
findings.ca_experience: A CA passing a provision entry cannot attach the working paper or the vendor's debit note to the voucher, so the supporting document lives in a separate Documents area with no link to the entry that depends on it. At audit time the two have to be reassembled by hand.
findings.market_standard: Tally attaches supporting files to a voucher. Zoho Books attaches up to five files per journal entry and shows them on the voucher.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an attachment control to JournalEditor that uploads to the existing Documents bucket and sends [{name, url}] in the create/update payload; render the list read-only on a posted entry.

findings.title: GET /api/accounting/ledger-span raises instead of degrading when there is no database, unlike every sibling report endpoint
findings.evidence: apps/api/routers/accounting.py:914-935 `get_ledger_span` ends with `from core.supabase_client import get_supabase` … `ledger_span(get_supabase(), ...)` with no `_prod_db()` None check, while every neighbour guards — e.g. :523-535 (`db = _prod_db(); if not db: raise 404`), :605-611 (`if not db: return api_response(True, {...})`), :645-648. apps/api/core/supabase_client.py:98-101 raises RuntimeError when SUPABASE_URL is unset.
findings.ca_experience: Only reachable in a deployment or dev environment without a database, where the reporting screens degrade gracefully and this one 500s — so 'All Time' on the period picker breaks the whole reports tab rather than falling back to the financial year.
findings.market_standard: n/a — internal consistency defect.
findings.suggested_fix: `db = _prod_db(); if db is None: return api_response(True, {"first_entry_date": None, "last_entry_date": None})` — the service already treats that pair as 'no span' and callers fall back to the FY.

findings.title: entry_date is an unvalidated string on the journal models, so a malformed date reaches the database (and, in mock mode, the ledger)
findings.evidence: apps/api/models/accounting.py:97 `entry_date: str  # YYYY-MM-DD` and :79 `entry_date: Optional[str] = None      # YYYY-MM-DD` — no validator, unlike the FYLabel discipline CLAUDE.md mandates for financial-year parameters (apps/api/models/fy.py). apps/api/services/manual_journal_service.py:57-62 checks only that entry_date is truthy. The kernel parses it defensively — apps/api/services/phase2_journal_service.py:1570-1573 `try: _d = _date.fromisoformat(...) except (TypeError, ValueError): _d = None` — and on failure simply SKIPS the client year-lock check rather than refusing.
findings.ca_experience: A malformed date from an integration or a mistyped payload either 500s at the database, or (worse) parses as None in the kernel and silently bypasses the client year lock, letting a posting into a closed year through.
findings.market_standard: n/a — input validation.
findings.suggested_fix: Give entry_date a field_validator that parses ISO YYYY-MM-DD (or a datetime.date type), and change the kernel's except branch to raise rather than skip the lock check — an unparseable date should never be the reason a lock is not applied.

maturity.rationale: The engine underneath is genuinely strong and, in places, better than the market: one posting kernel that asserts double-entry balance in integer paise and refuses a zero-value entry, an atomic SECURITY DEFINER RPC that also enforces firm, client-assignment and internal-client rules server-side, four immutability triggers with exactly one audited carve-out, a period-lock rule written once in SQL and shared by the screen and the write path, an append-only reversal keyed on the entry id, a soft delete that snapshots the whole entry with resolved account names, and a monthly passbook with a nightly re-derive-and-heal auditor. The reasoning is unusually well recorded — several migrations name the incident that motivated them. What holds it back from an A is that the layer a CA actually touches has not caught up with the engine. Three things are outright broken or unusable in production (year-end adjustment posting cannot write a row; cash receipts and payments book to Bank; the audit log is capped at 200 firm-wide rows with no per-entry history), three market-standard structures are simply absent (chart-of-accounts groups, day book, cost centres and bill-wise references), three accounting-hub features live in browser localStorage, and the Trial Balance is inception-to-date under an FY label. None of those is a flaw in the ledger; all of them are the difference between a correct ledger and a ledger a CA will run a practice on.
maturity.would_a_ca_buy_this_module_alone: Not yet — the kernel would survive a statutory audit, but a Tally user opens it, finds no day book, no group tree, no way to add a single ledger, cash payments landing in the bank account and a trial balance that adds up last year's sales to this year's, and closes it inside ten minutes.

open_questions_for_owner: Cost centres and bill-wise references are the two Tally features whose absence most often ends a migration conversation, and both are structural (a dimension column on journal_lines; a reference ledger keyed to documents). Are they in scope for this product, or is the positioning explicitly 'we replace Tally for compliance-led SME books, not for Tally power users'? The answer changes the shape of journal_lines and should be settled before more is built on it.

Is a party (customer/vendor) meant to become a GL ledger under a Sundry Debtors/Creditors group, as in Tally, or to stay a master record behind a single control account, as today? Party-wise ledger, party-wise trial balance and day-one bill-wise ageing all follow from that one decision.

There are three competing Schedule III classification mechanisms — account_subtype substring scanning (the live statements), chart_of_accounts.schedule_iii_mapping (a screen that changes nothing) and account_group_mappings (the year-end statements). Which one is authoritative, and who owns retiring the other two?

How much of the pillar is the analytics layer versus the ledger? The reporting engine is fast and correct, but there is no day book, no drill-through from a report line to a voucher, and no per-entry edit history — three cheap changes that would each be felt on every screen. Should those come before the structural work above?

The kernel enforces the client year lock but the filed-return lock lives only on two document routers. Should the filed-return gate become a hard refusal on every posting path, or a warning-with-override? A CA legitimately posts a June correction after GSTR-3B is filed, and then amends in July — a hard block would be wrong for that case and right for most others.

Recurring journals, budgets and retainers are per-browser localStorage today. Are these intended product features (in which case they need tables, RLS and a scheduler) or prototypes that should be removed from the Accounting hub until they are real? Leaving them advertised as firm registers is the worst of the three options.

Multi-currency is five phases deep and cannot be enabled without direct SQL. Is this a deliberate hold pending a paying export client, or an unfinished last mile? A single Partner-gated toggle would make it sellable; leaving it dark makes the investment invisible.

Once a client's year is locked by a year-end engagement there is no way back. Who should be allowed to reopen — Partner only, Partner with the firm lock PIN, or Partner with a written reason recorded on the engagement? The audit row already exists; only the policy is undecided.
strengths: ONE posting kernel, and the invariants are real. apps/api/services/phase2_journal_service.py:1543-1552 refuses an unbalanced journal and refuses a balanced-but-zero one before anything is written; every amount is integer paise; the (firm, client, reference_no, entry_date) idempotency fast path at :1611-1636 is backed by a real UNIQUE index rather than trusting the SELECT.

The atomic RPC is a genuine security boundary, not just a transaction. apps/api/migrations/271_post_journal_atomic_security_definer.sql:103-123 re-checks the caller's firm, runs can_access_client on the entry's client, and makes the firm's own internal client Partner-only — inside the database, so it holds regardless of which application path called it. :126-138 re-asserts Dr=Cr and the zero-value refusal, and :146-164 turns a concurrent duplicate into the winning entry's id instead of an error.

Immutability with exactly one audited carve-out, argued from the statute. apps/api/migrations/266_editable_journals_until_locked_or_filed.sql amends BOTH historical triggers (055's and 058's) rather than one, explains why amending one alone produces a carve-out that never fires, and fixes a latent bug where a BEFORE DELETE trigger's bare `RETURN NEW` silently cancelled draft deletions. The edit flag is a transaction-local GUC only a SECURITY DEFINER function can set.

The edit log covers the money, not just the header. Migration 266 attaches audit_capture_journal_line to journal_lines and resolves firm_id through the parent entry — because journal_lines has no firm_id and the generic trigger would have written nothing forever while every schema dump showed an audit trigger present.

Deletion snapshots the whole entry with account names. apps/api/migrations/276_delete_journal_pairs_and_snapshot_the_money.sql:104-124 writes the entry, its lines and each line's account_code and account_name into audit_log in the same transaction, and lets a reversed entry and its reversal go together (which strands nothing and nets to zero) while refusing either half alone with a message naming the other.

One period-lock rule, written once, shared by screen and write path. public.period_lock_reason (apps/api/migrations/267_period_lock_reason_for_every_document.sql) returns the REASON, not a boolean, so the CA is told 'GSTR-3B covering this date was filed on 18 Jul 2026' rather than being shown a disabled button; apps/api/services/manual_journal_service.py:167-182 and services/period_lock_service.py:53-70 both fail CLOSED if the check itself cannot run.

The reporting passbook obeys the house performance rule and proves itself. account_period_balances (migrations 227/228) is maintained by triggers on both the line-insert and the draft→posted paths, and apps/api/services/balance_cache_service.py:66-80 audit_client re-derives every bucket from the raw ledger; apps/api/jobs/scheduler.py:301-313 runs audit_and_heal_firm nightly with a recorded outcome, so a maintenance bug cannot silently corrupt a report.

The opening-balance engine is delta-based and leg-scoped, with the incident recorded. apps/api/services/opening_balance_service.py's module docstring records a real case where saving a bank account reversed 40.54 lakh of opening Trade Payables out of the GL, and the scope parameter (:155-217) exists so a side-effect sync can only touch the leg it changed. Deltas keep immutability without reversal-pair clutter.

Reversal is keyed on the entry id, not the reference. apps/api/services/phase2_journal_service.py:1799-1807 explains why: REV-{ref} let a second same-day cancellation dedup onto the first document's reversal. The is_reversed stamp moved into post_journal_atomic (migration 274) so the reversal and its flag cannot diverge, and :1821-1830 records the 42501 failure that motivated it.

Receipt and payment journals cannot be reversed through the generic journal endpoint. apps/api/routers/accounting.py:770-780 refuses an entry_type of Receipt or Payment and names the correct cascade endpoint, because reversing the journal alone would leave the sub-ledger allocations un-rolled-back.

Trial-balance import posts a REAL opening journal under its own source family. apps/api/services/trial_balance_import_service.py's header records that the old wizard wrote opening_balance_dr/cr_paise onto chart_of_accounts — columns no migration created and nothing read — and TB_SOURCE = 'TrialBalance' keeps it out of opening_balance_service's family so a customer edit cannot silently back it out.

The ledger is paged in SQL with a correct running balance. apps/api/domain/reporting/service.py:235-260 computes the window over the account's whole history and slices afterwards (public.account_ledger_page, migration 283), with a mock-mode Python twin held identical by tests/test_account_ledger_sql_parity_pg.py — the parity-test discipline CLAUDE.md prescribes.

Direct browser writes to chart_of_accounts are role-guarded in RLS, and the backlog is a test. apps/api/tests/test_direct_write_tables_are_role_guarded.py:40 lists chart_of_accounts among the tables migration 260 covers, and AWAITING_DECISION/CANNOT_SUCCEED are both empty with a test that fails the moment a new unguarded direct write appears.

The frontend genuinely keeps accounting logic out. apps/web/components/journal/JournalEditor.tsx:27-31 states the balance check is input validation only, and the ledger drill-down (apps/web/app/clients/[id]/accounting/page.tsx:942-945) and trial balance (:1167-1169) both note that opening/running/closing and both bases are computed server-side. Amounts are parsed once through lib/money/rupeeInput, and unparseable cells are surfaced per line rather than folded into 0.
subsystem: Accounting core: posting kernel, journals, chart of accounts, opening balances, financial years, period/year lock, manual journals, reversals, multi-currency, audit log
test_coverage_notes:
Volume is high and the shape is right for the kernel. 605 test modules under apps/api/tests, of which ~55 touch this subsystem by name (journal, opening, period, year_lock, coa, trial, audit, currency, reversal). I ran 156 of them in mock mode this session and all passed: test_journal_edit_until_locked, test_manual_journal, test_discard_draft_journal, test_journal_draft_workflow (52 passed), plus test_accounting_journal, test_opening_balance_journal, test_trial_balance_import_service, test_year_lock_management, test_client_year_lock_enforced, test_reversal_service, test_journal_reversal_kernel, test_coa_architecture (104 passed).

What is well covered: the kernel's balance and zero-value refusals; the draft→post workflow; reversal through the kernel and the is_reversed stamp (test_reversal_stamps_original_pg); line immutability against real Postgres (test_r251_journal_line_immutability_pg); the edit-until-locked rule in both mock and real-PG form (test_journal_edit_until_locked, test_r266_journal_edit_until_locked_pg, which even asserts the migration applied and its four functions exist); discard with pairs (test_discard_manual_journal_pg); the opening-balance delta engine and its date rule; the trial-balance import's separation from the opening family; five multi-currency phase suites. The cross-cutting schema tests are a real asset: test_backend_columns_exist_pg, test_frontend_columns_exist_pg, test_schema_matches_production_pg and test_guards_match_production_pg all compare code against a migration-built database and against dated production snapshots.

Where the coverage is thin, and it maps almost exactly onto the findings:

1. The FakeDB accepts any column, so a write naming a non-existent column passes green. apps/api/tests/test_r240_year_end_critical_gaps.py:324-341 asserts `len(db.rows("journal_entries")) == 1` for a payload that cannot be inserted into the real table (ACC-01). The one test that should have caught it, test_backend_columns_exist_pg, cannot see the payload because apps/api/tests/_backend_query_parser.py:230 only inspects inline `ast.Dict` literals and the call is `.insert(journal_entry)` on a variable — a known and documented budget, but this is what it costs.

2. Nothing exercises the edit path against a NON-manual entry. tests/test_journal_edit_until_locked.py:130 and tests/test_r266_journal_edit_until_locked_pg.py:107 both seed `source_type='manual'`, so the missing guard in edit_posted_journal (ACC-04) is invisible. The mirror-image discard rule IS pinned (migration 275's manual-only check).

3. No test posts a cash receipt or cash payment and asserts which GL account the money lands in (ACC-02/ACC-03) — the journal-shape tests assert Dr/Cr balance, not account identity by payment mode.

4. No test discards a draft and then calls post_draft (ACC-15), which is a two-line test that would have caught the missing `deleted_at` in journal_posting_service._SELECT.

5. No test asserts what a Trial Balance for a specific financial year should contain when the client has two years of books (ACC-08).

I found no test asserting a WRONG statutory behaviour in this subsystem. The statutory reasoning that IS tested — Rule 3(1)'s edit log presuming entries can change, the period lock's two limbs, integer paise everywhere — is correct and is argued in the migrations rather than assumed. The gap is not wrong assertions; it is that the mock-mode suite's test double is more permissive than Postgres, so the classes of bug that only Postgres rejects (missing NOT NULL columns, non-existent columns behind a variable) survive a green run.
what_exists:
A complete double-entry general ledger, client-scoped inside a firm tenant, with one posting kernel.

The GL is journal_entries + journal_lines (migration 003). Every accounting event routes through phase2_journal_service._create_journal (apps/api/services/phase2_journal_service.py:1506-1750): it asserts Σdebit = Σcredit in integer paise, refuses a zero-value entry, checks the client's year lock, resolves currency metadata (dormant unless three gates are on), dedupes on (firm, client, reference_no, entry_date), and inserts header plus lines in one server-side transaction via the post_journal_atomic RPC (migrations 152/243/271), which re-checks firm, client-assignment and the Partner-only internal client inside the database. Kernel methods exist for sales invoices, receipts, credit/debit notes (sales and purchase), purchase bills, purchase payments, payroll accrual/disbursement/settlement, fixed-asset acquisition/depreciation/disposal, and bank transactions. Accounts are resolved by system_account_key first, then by an ILIKE name pattern (:1404-1466).

Manual journals go through the same kernel (services/manual_journal_service.py), draft or posted, with attachments and per-line narration. A draft is approved through journal_posting_service.post_draft, which fires deferred bank settlement. A posted entry may be corrected while its period is open via the edit_posted_journal SQL function (migration 266), which re-checks both dates against the period lock, re-asserts Dr=Cr, rewrites the lines, rebuilds the reporting passbook and asserts no drift — atomically. Deletion is a soft delete through discard_posted_journal (275/276), manual entries only, with the whole entry and its account names snapshotted to audit_log; a reversed entry and its reversal can go together. Reversal is append-only through the kernel, keyed on the original entry's id.

Two locks: a firm-wide, PIN-guarded FY lock (firms.locked_financial_years, year_lock_service, Partner-gated endpoint, DB trigger blocking every other writer) and a per-client year lock written when a year-end engagement is finalised (client_year_locks, migration 289) enforced inside the kernel. A third gate, public.period_lock_reason (267), returns a sentence when a period is closed by a lock or by a filed return.

The chart of accounts is firm-level (migration 057), seeded flat with 53 Schedule III-shaped accounts (coa_seed_service). Opening balances reach the GL two ways: append-only deltas from customer/vendor/bank masters (opening_balance_service) and a trial-balance CSV import posting under its own journal family.

Reporting reads a trigger-maintained monthly passbook (account_period_balances, 227/228) with a nightly re-derive-and-heal audit, serving trial balance, P&L, balance sheet, cash flow, Schedule III, ageing and ratios. Screens: /accounting (firm hub), /accounting/{account-groups, coa-import, coa-export, lock-year, trial-balance-import, schedule-iii-mapping, recurring, budget, retainer}, and the client workspace at /clients/[id]/accounting with Journal, Ledger, Trial Balance, P&L, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow, FX and approval-queue tabs, plus a journal editor at /clients/[id]/accounting/journal/[entryId]/edit.
